newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovene PM welcomes EU entry talks invitation.
newsitem.headline: Slovene PM welcomes EU entry talks invitation.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek on Friday welcomed the news that the European Commission would recommend entry talks with Slovenia.
"We achieved our goal as joining the European Union is of vital economic interest and is therefore our priority," Drnovsek told a news conference.

On Thursday, European Commission officals said the commission planned to invite the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, Slovenia, Estonia and Cyprus to start negotiations on full membership early next year.
The commission is expected to offically reveal its decision on Wednesday.

Drnovsek pointed out that the commission placed Slovenia in the group on the assumption that it would immediately amend its constitution in line with EU demands and ratify the association agreement with the bloc.

"In my meetings with the European statesmen they all pointed out to me that changing the constitution and ratification of the EU agreement were preconditions for Slovenia to be included in the first round," he said.
Parliament needs to change the constitution in order to enable foreigners to buy land.
"At the moment Slovenia is in the best economic position of all candidates for EU membership," he added.
Slovenia, which broke away from the former Yugoslavia after a short but bloody conflict in 1991, had a GDP per capita of $9,362 in 1996.
